title: Time-dependent killing — beta-lactam regimen
context: A beta-lactam antibiotic shows TIME-dependent (time-above-MIC-driven) bacterial killing with little post-antibiotic effect, and a short plasma half-life (~1 h). Efficacy correlates with the fraction of the dosing interval that free drug stays above the MIC.
decision_required: Which dosing regimen maximizes efficacy for this PK/PD profile? Finish with a DECISION block: verdict: <frequent_or_continuous | high_dose_extended_interval>.

evidence.note: Time>MIC-driven (beta-lactams) → maximize time above MIC via frequent dosing or continuous/prolonged infusion. NOT once-daily high-dose (that is for concentration-dependent agents).

source: Standard PK/PD of antibacterials (time- vs concentration-dependent killing). Objective principle.

title: Concentration-dependent killing — aminoglycoside regimen
context: An aminoglycoside shows CONCENTRATION-dependent killing (Cmax/MIC-driven) with a prolonged post-antibiotic effect; higher peaks mean more rapid, complete kill, while toxicity is driven by accumulation at the renal tubule over time.
decision_required: Which dosing regimen best fits this PK/PD profile? Finish with a DECISION block: verdict: <frequent_or_continuous | high_dose_extended_interval>.

evidence.note: Cmax/MIC-driven with post-antibiotic effect (aminoglycosides) → once-daily / extended-interval high-dose to maximize peak and allow a trough that limits renal accumulation/toxicity.

source: Standard PK/PD of aminoglycosides (extended-interval dosing). Objective principle.

title: Long half-life — loading dose?
context: A drug has a long terminal half-life (~40 h), so at a fixed maintenance dose it would take roughly a week (4-5 half-lives) to reach steady-state therapeutic concentrations. The clinical situation requires therapeutic levels quickly.
decision_required: Should the regimen include a loading dose? Finish with a DECISION block: verdict: <loading_dose_then_maintenance | maintenance_only>.

evidence.note: Long half-life + need for rapid onset → a loading dose achieves target concentration immediately; maintenance alone takes ~4-5 half-lives (days) to reach steady state.
